text:
Maya: quick Q — noticed a weird combo: stop sequences sometimes cause the model to return fewer logprobs than tokens when streaming + max_tokens set. Is that expected?
Liu: can you paste a minimal repro?
Maya: repro:
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "rnwd-2b",
  "prompt": "Count: 1\n2\n3\n",
  "max_tokens": 1,
  "stop": ["\n"],
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```
Maya: streaming returns the newline as stop but logprobs is empty for final token sometimes.
Jon: hmm. Current semantic: stop sequence termination is applied before enforcing max_tokens? or after? We should be explicit in contract.
Tim: my take: evaluation order is: generate tokens until stop matched OR tokens_generated >= max_tokens. If stop matched, we should return tokens up to but excluding stop delimiter; logprobs should be for all returned tokens. If we cut because max_tokens hit, logprobs may be partial for last token if streaming truncated. We need to define streaming truncation behavior.
Liu: agreed. We have two edgecases: (A) stop matches mid-token boundary with byte/utf8 issues, (B) streaming chunk cut before we can compute full logprobs for last token.
Elena: proposal: API contract: 1) stop sequences take precedence over further token emission — generator stops as soon as a stop is detected (and that stop is not part of returned text). 2) max_tokens is a hard cap on produced tokens; if max_tokens is reached exactly when a stop would have been found later, max_tokens wins. 3) logprobs must be present for every returned token; if streaming truncation prevents computing logprobs for the last returned token, respond with null for that token's logprobs and include an explicit warning in top-level `warnings` list (canonical code `incomplete_logprobs_streaming`).
Maya: I like explicit warning. any objections?
Jon: fine, but we can't change top-level schema ad-hoc. Maybe reuse `warnings` list we already have in responses.
Tim: yes let's put `warnings: ["incomplete_logprobs_streaming"]` with canonical code.
Liu: also add note about temp/top_p interplay: when temperature=0 and top_p<1 behavior should be deterministic; document that logging may omit distribution if deterministic path uses argmax and we don't compute full softmax.
Elena: ok action items: (1) update API contract doc with ordering + warnings (2) add unit test that repros Maya's snippet (3) runtime: ensure streaming computes logprobs for emitted tokens or attaches warning.
Maya: I'll file a quick PR to docs and add the unit test. ping @Jon for review when ready.
Jon: will review, TY. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary for runtime patch at 03:30 UTC
Maya: thanks — keeping this async so eng-oncall doesn't get paged.
Tim: small note: also record behavior for `stop` matching multiple alternatives; prefer earliest match by token end position.
Liu: yep. last: dataset note — some customers send stop as \r\n; add normalization doc.
Maya: cool. I'll add all these to the PR.
